baseRevisionNote: dev tip the branch was cut from; the fix commits are recorded below by their own shas once made
scope: every finding recorded by the v0.9.0 adversarial review (t6: F1-F7), the t7 prose item, and the one known gap recorded after that wave (pooled write tasks reaching read-only members)
notFixed: packages/mpd-mcp-shared ships no README — not a defect: the directory has no package.json and is not a workspace member (it is the shared binary resolver module, documented by the MCP packages that consume it and by AGENTS.md §12)
host-limited verifications carried over from v0.9.0 (pnpm-path packed install, bun run test:qa:all, Web GUI, cross-platform) stay unverified on this host — unchanged by this wave

findings.defect: a failed skill enumeration returned an ARRAY, which the harness reads as {candidates, complete:true} and CACHES per (cwd, scope, revision) — one transient failure hid a provider's skills until a restart
findings.fix: emit()/list() now return {candidates: [], complete: false} on an enumeration failure (data-level per-candidate skips stay complete:true, they are permanent until the files change)

red.test: F3: an enumeration failure is reported as an INCOMPLETE observation, never a cacheable empty catalog

findings.defect: skill-name collisions were never recorded: the project provider had no onSkip and the view had no cross-extension skill annotation, so mpd_ext_list claimed skills the harness does not serve (and a NON-extension collision — the corpus — was invisible)
findings.fix: (a) the project provider records its skips keyed by (workspace dir, candidate name) and snapshot() attributes them to the owning entry; (b) annotateSkillSurfaces records an extension-vs-extension collision on the loser with the winner and both ranks; (c) mpd_ext_list/mpd_ext_show read the harness's own catalog (dsh.listSkills) and report every claim as served/notServed with a checked/reason envelope

tests: F4: a same-name skill claimed by two extensions is reported on the loser WITH the winner and both ranks
F4: a claim the catalog resolves to a NON-extension provider is reported as not served
F4: a duplicate project-plane skill name is attributed to the PROJECT entry that claims it

findings.source: t6 review, packages/mpd-ext-plugin/src/mcp.ts:342,348 (deviation introduced by the plan's own REV4 wording)
findings.defect: an unsupported or lossy advertised outputSchema dropped the WHOLE TOOL, where the harness posture drops only the SCHEMA and keeps the tool (H/dsh-mcp-client supportedOutputSchema)
findings.fix: keep the tool, drop structuredContent, record the reason as a per-tool note ('downgraded' in the server's warn line); only an unprojectable inputSchema still skips its tool

red.test: an unsupported outputSchema drops the SCHEMA and keeps the tool, while an unprojectable inputSchema skips its tool

findings.source: t6 review, packages/mpd-ext-plugin/src/mcp.ts:319-328 vs the contract's sanitizer policy
findings.defect: a non-object-rooted foreign inputSchema was passed through as `parameters` (measured: projectSchema({type:'string'}) -> {type:'string'}), so the tool's arguments could not be described at all
findings.fix: objectRootedSchema() normalizes a non-object root onto an object carrying the payload under a single `value` property (annotations stay with the payload), validates the result against the harness subset, and records the downgrade as a note

red.test: a non-object-rooted inputSchema is normalized onto an object root instead of being passed through
red.observed: parameters were the scalar/array schema itself

findings.defect: `cwdOf(listOptions) ?? dsh.workspaceRoot()` fell back to DSH_WORKSPACE_ROOT and then process.cwd(): the project plane could serve ANOTHER project's extensions, and the apply-time shadow guard could hide a host-wide extension because of a workspace the caller never named
findings.fix: the project plane requires the caller's cwd (no fallback; an unknown cwd means 'no project plane'); the apply-time shadow guard is SKIPPED when the caller names no workspace (a guess can only hide live content)

tests: F5: a provider call with NO cwd serves nothing from the project plane (never process.cwd())
F5: with no cwd a host-wide extension is SERVED, not silently shadowed by a guessed workspace

findings.defect: mpd_ext_show echoed the raw descriptor, including author-declared MCP `env` VALUES — exactly where an API key lives — into the session log and the model's context
findings.fix: redactedDescriptor() masks every env value as <redacted> (keys stay: they are the interface)

red.test: F6: mpd_ext_show redacts author-declared env VALUES in the echoed descriptor
red.observed: the secret value appeared verbatim in the tool result

findings.source: t6 review, registry.ts annotateRoleSurfaces 'known residual' (and the same gap for skills)
findings.defect: the whole-view claim maps only knew the DESCRIPTOR `enabled` flag, so a CONFIG-disabled extension still claimed its role (and skill) names and a later claimant was reported refused while the roster would have exposed it
findings.fix: registry.view() takes the caller's EFFECTIVE enabled predicate and passes it to both annotations; the 'disabled' note now says WHICH kind of disable it is, and role/skill notes are re-derived by reason prefix instead of by item name

red.test: F7: a CONFIG-disabled extension claims no role name, so the next claimant is exposed
red.observed: beta-on was refused with the refusal note; contributions.roles was 0

findings.source: known gap recorded after the v0.9.0 wave (occurred twice: tasks t15/t16)
findings.defect: the scheduler's pool branch had no capability test, so a read-only member (the roster's read-only roles carry the seven write-capable names in toolDeny) was handed a pooled implementation/repair task it could not execute
findings.fix: nextCapableTask (regions mpd-delta pool-capability-guard/-select in lib/scheduler.js): the member's OWN task still dispatches (loudly, including when its toolDeny blocks it), a pooled task it cannot run stays IN THE POOL and the withholding is logged once per (team, member, reason)

red.observed: nextCapableTask does not exist in the pre-fix module (0 pass / 7 fail)

findings.defect: a terminal task record's objective still says 'five tools' while the binding acceptance line, plan §1.5 and the frozen contract all say FOUR
findings.fix: recorded, not amended (the task is terminal and immutable): re-checked that no HUMAN-facing doc claims five — docs/extensions.md:400 and its zh pair already state four shipped / a fifth (mpd_ext_reload) cut, which is the honest history

red.observed: n/a — prose-only item, no behaviour to reproduce

green.observed: grep over README.md, docs/*.md (EN+zh) and packages/*/README*.md finds no 'five tools' claim

gates.evidence: raw/mount-extension-lifecycle.log + ../extension-lifecycle/2026-09-15T01-16-15.149Z (all four tools offered AND called; failure/isolation arms ok; packed arm GREEN, owner t11)

redMeasurement.method: a detached git worktree at the pre-fix revision (d6a6f59) with ONLY the three post-fix test files copied in, run as `bun test --cwd <worktree> <abs path>`
redMeasurement.whyCwd: measured trap: without --cwd a relative test path is also resolved against the MAIN checkout, so the same file is loaded twice (once pre-fix, once post-fix) and the verdict is worthless — the first RED attempt showed '90 tests across 2 files' for a single-file argument and was discarded
